topic.title: One million people are now Myntra's sales force
topic.claim: I think the real Diwali campaign this year isn't the TV ad, it's a million people tagging products on their own Instagram for a cut of the sale.
topic.behaviour: Myntra's Instagram affiliate programme crossed 1 million creator sign-ups with 200,000 creators actively posting tagged content and roughly 3 million affiliate posts created so far, expected to roughly double this festive season. Amazon's India Influencer Program has doubled to 200,000 creators, with creator-led purchases up 107% and per-creator earnings up 60%, and about 75% of participating creators and nearly 70% of buyers coming from non-metro India. Festive creator marketing spend overall is projected at Rs 900 crore this Diwali, up from Rs 700 crore last year, across 7,200 brands.
topic.mechanism: Affiliate commerce works better than paid sponsorship because the creator is actually earning off the sale, not the post, so they push harder and the follower trusts it more. And it's spreading in small towns first because that's where a side income from your phone actually changes your month.
topic.group: brand marketers and small creators chasing Diwali side income
real_details: Myntra's Instagram affiliate programme crossed 1 million creator sign-ups, 200,000 creators actively publishing, ~3 million affiliate posts since launch
Amazon's India Influencer Program doubled to 200,000 creators, creator-led purchases up 107%, per-creator earnings up 60%
40 million shoppers influenced Jan-Sep 2026, up 65% YoY
~75% of participating creators and ~70% of buyers from non-metro India
Festive creator spend projected at Rs 900 crore in 2026 (up from Rs 700 crore), across 7,200 brands vs 6,000 last year, top 10-15% of brands accounting for ~65% of spend
topic.news_peg: Myntra affiliate programme crossing 1 million sign-ups and Amazon doubling to 200,000 creators, both reported October 2026, ahead of Diwali on November 8, 2026
topic.why_now: Three separate reports this month all point to the same shift right as festive spending peaks

score.why: Turns the Diwali 'campaign' into ordinary people doing unpaid affiliate work, straight out of her 'influencer marketing is unmeasured reach' belief.

edits: slide 3: cut 'Two platforms, one idea: pay people per sale, not per post.' Slide 4 makes the same point.
slide 8: cut 'without a salary or a Diwali bonus'. Slide 2 already made the 'sales force nobody had to hire' point.
slide 9: cut 'More of your friends are on commission than you think.' It restates the hook and reads like a tidy moral; end on 'This Diwali, your feed is the shop.'

paragraphs: Over a million Indians just signed up to sell Myntra clothes on their own Instagram. And the people they're selling to are you.
Swipe to read →
Myntra's Instagram affiliate programme crossed a million sign-ups. You tag a product, someone buys, you get a cut.
Around 200,000 are already posting. That's a sales force nobody had to hire.
Amazon is doing the same thing more quietly. Its India Influencer Program doubled to 200,000 creators.
Purchases through creators went up 107%. What each creator earns went up 60%.
I've sat through enough brand calls about influencer budgets. A sponsored post gets paid whether anyone buys or not. Everyone in the room knows it.
Affiliate flips that. The creator eats only when you check out.
So they push harder. The kurta gets a try-on reel, a close-up, a link in bio.
You trust it more because she's your cousin's college friend. She's also more of a salesperson than any celebrity in the TV ad.
Now look where it's growing. About 75% of Amazon's creators are from non-metro India. Nearly 70% of buyers too.
That's where a few thousand rupees from your phone actually changes the month. It's the scooty EMI sorted.
The big money is still there. Creator spend this Diwali is projected at Rs 900 crore, up from Rs 700 crore.
The top 10-15% of brands take about 65% of it. For everyone else, paying per sale looks a lot smarter.
I find this funny. A million people just joined a brand's sales team.
And the market they sell to is their own followers. Mostly friends, cousins and old classmates.
Next time a friend's story says "loving this kurta", check for the little tag.
This Diwali, your feed is the shop.

hook_candidates.hook: Over a million Indians just signed up to sell Myntra clothes on their own Instagram. And the people they're selling to are you.
Imagine a sales team of a million people. Nobody hired them. And every one of them is selling to you through their stories.
This Diwali's best salesperson is your cousin's college friend. I know how that sounds. Wait till you see how she gets paid.
Your friend's Diwali kurta reel looks like she's just showing off her outfit. Look closer. There's a reason she posted it.
I have a prediction. This Diwali, you'll buy more from your friends' Instagram stories than from any TV ad.

sources.fact: Myntra's Instagram affiliate programme recorded over 1 million sign-ups within a month of launch, with 200,000 creators already posting and about 3 million posts across Instagram and Facebook. Myntra expects creator posts to double this festive season.
